senses.definition: The one main goal that guides all other decisions.
senses.caution: There should be only one, and a deck with three suggests the team has not chosen. It sets a direction, so avoid presenting it as a quarterly target you do not fully control.
senses.example: Time to a trustworthy answer is our north star for the year. If a feature does not move that, it waits.

cues.text: Three workstreams each have their own definition of success, and you want one outcome put above all of them and held there for the year.
A sponsor asks how you will choose between two features when both look good on paper, and you want to name the single measure that settles it.

You and your partner are weighing two cities, two jobs and a school, and you want to agree in advance on the one thing that matters most, so the decision is not made by whoever argues hardest at the time.
A friend is drowning in options for the year ahead and asks how you decide anything, and your honest answer is that you fix one thing and let everything else bend around it.

distractors: The one currently most likely to win, said while the outcome is still open.
A number given straight, with the caveats stripped out.
The underlying layer everything above it runs on.
Real agreement from the people you need.
The most senior people, as one group.
